main_text.l: Rhabarbarū, Dosis ad.3 iiij. v.aut sex.

Agaricum est familiaris medicina, ubi correcta fuerit. corrigitur autem cum oxymelite scyllitico, aut sale gemmæ, uel zingibere, semper admiscendo tertiam partem: & quia uentriculo aduersatur sua leuitate, debet admisceri aliqua medicina stomachica: sicut Cinnamomum, Garyophy. Mastix, aut calamus aromati. Dantur binæ drachmæ cum oxymelite, uel melle rosæ macerati. dosis ad 3.5. Potest dari in forma liquida, aut pilulari, uel pulueris.
Senna corrigitur cū zingibere, uel datur cū iure gallinæ, pulli, uel carnium, abstq; trituratione.

Rhabarbarū corrigitur cū tertia parte spicæ nardi, aut cinnamomi, uel iunci odorati, aut mastichis. Datur cū sero lactis, aut succo cichorij, uel cū decoctione purgate bilē flauā. Maceratur in ijsdē decoctis, aut in aquis distillatis, idq; in æstate: hyeme uerò in uino albo optimo. In substātia datur ad 3. iiij usque. Turbith
Et alia permulta super cineres calidos tēperantur aliquandiu humore siue liquore idoneo, ut uis uehemēs corrigatur.

page.notes: The brace at the right of the dose list groups the first items; the right-hand note "Et alia permulta super cineres calidos..." is set beside the brace and is given as a foot note. Some words in the running text are doubtful (e.g. "Garyophy", "Psyllium", "Scammonium") and were read from a slightly blurred scan. The final line "Turbith" is printed at the right foot and is treated as a catchword.
